qa_pairs.question: According to the age distribution chart and the marital status chart of people engaged in the legal service industry, which options can best explain why the young group stands out in this industry?

answer.A: The age distribution chart shows that the young group has a relatively high proportion and a significantly higher TGI value than other age groups. Meanwhile, in the marital status chart, the TGI value of the unmarried population is higher than that of the married population. This together indicates that the industry is more attractive to young and unmarried individuals.
answer.B: The age distribution chart shows that the TGI value of the 55 - 64 age group is the highest (65), while the TGI value of the young group is lower. Therefore, the middle - aged group is the most prominent.
answer.C: The young group stands out because the legal service industry requires high - intensity physical labor, and young people have more physical strength and energy, which applies to any industry.
answer.D: The unmarried population performs better because married people usually have family burdens, resulting in a decline in work efficiency. This is a common social phenomenon.
answer.E: In the marital status chart, the TGI value of the married population (60) is higher than that of the unmarried population (90), indicating that the married status can better enhance the industry performance, which has nothing to do with the young group.
answer.F: The age distribution chart shows that the TGI values of the young group (such as 18 - 24 years old and 25 - 34 years old) are much higher than the benchmark, and the TGI value of the unmarried population in the marital status chart is also relatively high, indicating that the young group is more likely to be unmarried, thus having stronger performance in this industry.

qa_pairs.question: Analyze the education level chart and the consumption level chart. Which patterns indicate that there may be a correlation between high education level and high - consumption habits in the industry?

answer.A: The consumption level chart shows that the low - consumption group has the highest proportion (20%), indicating that practitioners in the industry are generally thrifty, and education level has no impact on this.
answer.B: People with high education levels usually have higher incomes and therefore are more inclined to high - consumption. This is a common sense in social economy and has nothing to do with the specific industry.
answer.C: In the education level chart, the TGI value of people with a high - school education or below is the highest (140), while in the consumption level chart, the TGI value of the high - consumption group is relatively low (90), indicating that people with low education levels are more likely to have high - consumption.
answer.D: The education level chart shows that the TGI value of people with a bachelor's degree or above is significantly higher than the benchmark, and the TGI value of the high - consumption group in the consumption level chart is also relatively high, which implies that people with high education levels are more likely to have high - consumption habits, forming a common feature in this industry.
answer.E: Although the medium - consumption group has the highest proportion in the consumption level chart, the TGI value of the high - consumption group is higher than the benchmark. At the same time, the TGI value of people with high education levels in the education level chart is prominent, indicating that the industry characteristics are more inclined to attract individuals with high education levels and strong consumption abilities.
answer.F: In the consumption level chart, the TGI value of the medium - consumption group (90) is higher than that of the high - consumption group (110). At the same time, the education level chart shows that the TGI value of people with a junior - college degree is the highest (140). Therefore, the medium - consumption is most strongly associated with high education levels.

label: D

qa_pairs.question: The gender ratio chart shows that the TGI value of female practitioners is relatively high, but the marital status chart shows that the TGI value of married people is relatively low. Which options can reasonably reconcile this phenomenon?

answer.A: Combined with the age distribution chart, the 35 - 44 age group has the highest proportion (30%) and a high TGI value (120), and women may be concentrated in this age group. Therefore, the married status does not affect the performance of women.
answer.B: The high TGI value of female practitioners is because women are more careful and patient, which is suitable for the legal service industry. The low TGI value of married people is because marriage disperses energy, which is a common workplace rule.
answer.C: In the gender ratio chart, the TGI value of men (85) is higher than that of women (115). At the same time, in the marital status chart, the TGI value of the unmarried population is low (90), indicating that the unmarried male group performs better, which can explain the contradiction between the high TGI value of women and the low TGI value of married people.
answer.D: Combined with the marital status chart and the age distribution chart, the low TGI value of married people is consistent with the low TGI values of the middle - aged and above groups (such as 35 - 44 years old and 45 - 54 years old). It may be that married people are older, resulting in weaker performance, which indirectly indicates that the young and unmarried group (possibly including women) is more prominent.
answer.E: Combined with the gender ratio chart and the age distribution chart, the high TGI value of women is consistent with the high TGI values of the young group (such as 25 - 34 years old). It may be that women are more concentrated in these high - performing young groups, thus partially explaining the gender advantage.
answer.F: The low TGI value of married people indicates that family responsibilities affect work performance, which is true in all industries and has nothing to do with gender.

label: D
E
